name: Shades
title_tag: Custom Shades in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Find custom shades in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Compare Hunter Douglas fabrics and controls, with measuring and installation from Woodland Hills.

sections.title: Custom Shades in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Tell us where the sunlight bothers you, how much privacy you need and what you like about the room. We'll help you choose custom shades, measure your windows and take care of installation. Start with a visit to John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills, serving Los Angeles and the San Fernando Valley.

sections.title: Choose the room, choose the fabric
paragraphs: We start with how you use the room, when the sunlight is strongest and how much of the view you want to keep. A fabric that works well in the living room may let in too much light for a bedroom. Seeing the options together helps make those differences clear.

Roller shades, screen shades and honeycomb shades are a large part of our work. We've used solar mesh shades in Valley storefronts to help manage glare while keeping a view outside. At home, the same questions about light, privacy and everyday use help narrow the choices.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas shade collections
paragraphs: As a Hunter Douglas dealer, we can help you compare the collections by fabric, construction and control options. We also carry Alta shades if you'd like to compare another option for your project.

items.title: Roller and solar shades
items.text: Designer Roller Shades use a single fabric panel that rolls up at the top of the window. Designer Screen Shades help manage sun and glare while preserving a view out. Designer Banded Shades alternate sheer and solid bands. Alustra® Woven Textures® Roller Shades and Alustra® Architectural Roller Shades offer additional fabric textures and constructions to compare.

items.title: Cellular and honeycomb shades
items.text: Duette® Honeycomb Shades and Applause® Cellular Shades use cellular fabrics that add insulation at the window. Sonnette® Cellular Roller Shades combine cellular construction with a roller-style design. Each has its own fabric and operating choices to consider.

items.title: Sheer shades
items.text: Silhouette® Sheer Shades, Pirouette® Sheer Shades and Nantucket™ Sheer Shades use adjustable fabric vanes to change the light and view. Their fabrics and construction differ, so it helps to see how each one looks open and closed.

items.title: Roman shades
items.text: Vignette® Modern Roman Shades, Carole Fabrics® Roman Shades and Alustra® Woven Textures® Roman Shades give you a fabric treatment with folds. Compare the fold styles, fabrics and lining options, including how much of the window each treatment covers when raised.

items.title: Woven wood shades
items.text: Provenance® Woven Wood Shades bring natural woven materials to the window. The weave and lining affect how much you can see through, so we'll discuss privacy as well as texture. Alustra® Woven Textures® collections provide other woven-fabric choices in roller and Roman styles.

items.title: Vertical shades and panels
items.text: For wide windows and sliding doors, compare Luminette® Sheer Panels and Skyline® Gliding Window Panels. The opening direction, space for the panels to stack and clearance around door handles all matter.

sections.title: Daytime glare and nighttime privacy
paragraphs: A screen fabric can preserve your view during the day, but a lit room may be visible from outside after dark. If you need nighttime privacy, tell us before you settle on a fabric. We can discuss an additional privacy layer or a different shade configuration.
For a bedroom, we'll also look at room-darkening fabrics and the light that can enter around the edges. The fabric and the way the shade fits both matter.

sections.title: Measuring, installation and help afterward
paragraphs: Once you've chosen a shade, we take the measurements, check the mounting space and confirm the controls before ordering. At installation, we check operation and show you how to use the shades.
If a backorder changes the schedule, we'll keep you informed. If a question comes up after installation, you can contact us for help.

sections.title: Questions about custom shades

faqs.question: Can I motorize the shades I choose?
faqs.answer: Many collections offer motorized options. We'll confirm what's available for the specific product, window size and controls you want before you order.

faqs.question: Can I coordinate shades in different rooms?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can compare fabrics and colors across the rooms you're working on. That may mean using different shade types where the light, privacy or door access calls for it.

faqs.question: What affects the price?
faqs.answer: Window size, fabric, product construction and controls all affect the cost. After discussing your budget and choices, we take professional measurements and prepare a quote.

sections.title: See the shade options in Woodland Hills
paragraphs: Come in to compare fabrics, colors and finishes and talk through your rooms. If you're unsure where to start, tell us what you'd like to change about your current window coverings.

name: Blinds
title_tag: Custom Blinds in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Find custom blinds in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Compare Hunter Douglas wood, faux wood, metal and vertical blinds, measured and installed for you.

sections.title: Custom Blinds in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Blinds give you a simple way to adjust daylight and privacy throughout the day. At John Crawford Company, we'll help you compare materials, finishes and controls, then measure and install the blinds for your windows. Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to get started.

sections.title: Start with the material and how you'll use it
paragraphs: The room helps narrow the choices. You might want the grain of real wood in a living room, a moisture-resistant material in a bathroom or a vertical treatment that opens easily beside a sliding door.

Think about privacy, how often you open the windows and whether you prefer tilting the slats or raising the blind out of the way. From there, we can compare colors and finishes that work with the rest of the room.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas blinds to compare
paragraphs: See how the materials look with the slats or vanes open and closed. We carry Hunter Douglas and Alta blinds and can help you compare the choices for your windows.

items.title: Parkland® Wood Blinds
items.text: Real-wood slats with painted and stained finish choices. We can help you compare the wood tones with your trim, flooring and furniture.

items.title: EverWood® Alternative Wood Blinds
items.text: A faux wood option designed to resist warping and fading. For a bathroom or sunroom, we can help you compare its moisture and sunlight resistance with real wood.

items.title: Custom Metal Blinds
items.text: A metal-slat option with a wide selection of colors. Compare the available slat sizes and finishes, with attention to the space needed for mounting and operation.

items.title: Aria™ Soft Blinds
items.text: Fabric vanes give horizontal blinds a softer appearance and diffuse incoming light. Compare them with wood or metal if you'd like adjustable vanes with a fabric finish.

items.title: Custom Vertical Blinds
items.text: Vertical vanes provide adjustable light control for wide windows and sliding doors. We'll help you choose the material and decide which opening direction suits the way you use the room.

items.title: Skyline® Gliding Window Panels
items.text: Wide fabric panels travel along a track and stack to the side. Allowing space for the open panels is especially important at a doorway you use often.

items.title: Luminette® Sheer Panels
items.text: Vertical fabric vanes within sheer panels give you another way to manage light across large windows and doors. They also appear among the Hunter Douglas sheer-shade and drapery options.

sections.title: The fit matters when you open the window
paragraphs: Handles, locks, trim and window depth all affect the installation. A blind needs room to tilt, lift or slide without getting in the way of the window or door.

We check those details during professional measuring. Where there are several windows together, we also discuss the layout and how you'd like to operate them. That gives us a clear plan before anything is ordered.

sections.title: One window is welcome
paragraphs: You don't need a whole-house project to call us. If you're replacing a blind in one room, we'll help you choose for that window and explain the next steps.
For a larger project, we can work through the rooms together and compare where the same material makes sense and where you may want something different.

sections.title: Questions about blinds

faqs.question: What's the difference between wood and faux wood blinds?
faqs.answer: Real wood gives you natural grain and stained finish choices. Faux wood offers a wood-style appearance with different material properties, including moisture resistance. We'll help you compare them for the actual room.

faqs.question: Can blinds make a bedroom completely dark?
faqs.answer: Closed slats reduce incoming light, but light can still pass through gaps and around the edges. If a darker bedroom is your main goal, we'll discuss suitable shade or drapery options as well.

faqs.question: Can you repair a blind I already own?
faqs.answer: We can review the product and available components. Send a photo and describe the problem so we can assess whether repair is possible. Parts availability and the condition of the blind matter, including for products from other brands.

sections.title: Talk through your windows with us
paragraphs: Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to compare blind materials and finishes. We'll help you narrow the choices and arrange measuring and installation for your Los Angeles home.

name: Shutters
title_tag: Interior Shutters in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Explore custom interior shutters in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Compare Hunter Douglas wood, composite and vinyl collections in Woodland Hills.

sections.title: Custom Interior Shutters in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Shutters become part of the way a window looks and works. We'll help you choose the material, finish, louver size and panel arrangement, then take professional measurements and handle installation. Start at John Crawford Company's Woodland Hills showroom.

sections.title: Compare wood, composite and vinyl shutters
paragraphs: People often call this style plantation shutters. The material is one of the first choices to make. We'll consider sunlight, moisture and the finish you want, along with the window itself.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Heritance® Hardwood Shutters
items.text: Made from genuine hardwood, with painted and stained finishes. This is an option to explore when the character of real wood is part of what you want for the room.

items.title: Hunter Douglas NewStyle® Hybrid Shutters
items.text: A composite construction with the appearance of painted wood. We'll help you compare the finish and available panel configurations with the other shutter materials.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Palm Beach™ Polysatin™ Shutters
items.text: A water-resistant material designed for strong sunlight and moisture. It's an option to discuss for bathrooms and other rooms where exposure affects the material choice.

sections.title: Look at the panels as well as the louvers
paragraphs: Louver size changes the appearance of the shutter and the view when the louvers are open. Panel width and the number of panels affect how the shutters open into the room.

We check the depth of the window, projecting handles, nearby furniture and the room available for opening the panels. The frame can affect the fit and appearance, too. These choices are easier to settle before the shutters are ordered.

sections.title: Privacy, daylight and bedroom light
paragraphs: Tilting the louvers lets you change the amount of daylight and the view into the room. Closing them gives more privacy, while opening the panels exposes more of the window.

Shutters can darken a room, but light can still enter between louvers and around the panels. If keeping a bedroom dark is especially important, tell us early. We'll talk through what the shutter can do and whether another treatment would help.

sections.title: From measuring to the finished installation
paragraphs: John's background began with installation, and that experience still shapes how we look at a window. We check the mounting details and how the finished panels will operate before placing the order.
At installation, we check the fit and operation and show you how to use the shutters. Ask us about the panels, louvers or care instructions for the material you've chosen.

sections.title: Questions about interior shutters

faqs.question: Can shutters work on a door or an unusual window shape?
faqs.answer: Some collections offer door and specialty-shape configurations. We'll review the shape, dimensions, hardware and clearance to see which options are suitable.

faqs.question: Should I choose a larger louver?
faqs.answer: It depends on the look you prefer and the depth of the window. We'll show you the available sizes and consider the view, proportions and clearance together.

faqs.question: What affects the cost of custom shutters?
faqs.answer: The material, window size, panel arrangement, frame and finish all contribute. After professional measuring and product selection, we can prepare a quote for your windows.

sections.title: See the materials and finishes in person
paragraphs: Bring your ideas to our Woodland Hills showroom. We'll talk through the windows you're considering, compare the shutter choices and help you decide what to look at next.

name: Drapery
title_tag: Custom Drapery in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Plan custom drapery and curtains in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Explore fabrics, lining and hardware, with professional measuring and installation.

sections.title: Custom Drapery in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Choose drapery for the way you want the room to look and the way you need it to work. We'll help with fabric, lining, hardware and installation, whether you want curtains that close each evening or side panels to finish the window. Visit John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills to talk through your ideas.

sections.title: Decide what the drapery needs to do
paragraphs: Before choosing a fabric, we'll ask whether the panels need to move, how much light you want to control and what you want to see when they're open. Drapery that closes across a window needs enough fabric and space to operate properly. Stationary side panels serve a different purpose.
Lining, length and fullness deserve attention, too. Those choices affect how the fabric hangs, how much light comes through and how the finished drapery looks from inside and outside the room.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas drapery and related collections

items.title: Carole Fabrics® Custom Drapes
items.text: Carole Fabrics, a Hunter Douglas partner company, offers fabric choices for functioning drapery and stationary panels. We'll help compare color, pattern and texture, along with lining and heading styles.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Luminette® Sheer Panels
items.text: Sheer panels with adjustable vertical fabric vanes offer light control across wide windows and doors. This is another option to compare if you like a sheer appearance and want to adjust the view and privacy.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Provenance® Woven Wood Shades
items.text: The collection includes vertical woven options for a different texture at large openings. We'll review the available configurations, weave and privacy lining for the window or door you're working on.

sections.title: Give the hardware the same attention as the fabric
paragraphs: A rod or track needs to support the fabric and let it move the way you intend. We check the span, mounting points, brackets and the space the drapery occupies when open. On a wide opening, those details deserve attention early.
If you already have drapery and the rod or track is the problem, tell us what's happening. We can review the hardware and discuss whether repair or replacement is appropriate.

sections.title: Layer drapery with a shade or blind
paragraphs: You can use a shade for everyday light control and add drapery for fabric, privacy or room darkening. We'll look at how the layers fit together so the rod, fabric and window treatment have room to operate.
If several windows share a room, it helps to consider how the treatments look together when open and closed. You can coordinate fabrics without putting the same treatment on every opening.

sections.title: Measuring and installation for the whole arrangement
paragraphs: We take the measurements and confirm the fabric, hardware and mounting arrangement before the order is placed. At installation, we check the hang and operation and walk you through using the treatment.
One customer described the hardware side of a drapery project this way:

quote.text: Quick response by John to organize materials fabrication and excellent installation service by Max to replace damaged curtain rods in a 22 foot run of drapery. Highly recommended!
quote.author: Jan Edling, Google review

sections.title: Questions about custom drapery

faqs.question: Do I need drapes, curtains or side panels?
faqs.answer: The names overlap in everyday use. What matters is whether the fabric needs to open and close, provide privacy or finish the sides of the window. We'll start with those needs and show you suitable styles.

faqs.question: Can drapery help darken a bedroom?
faqs.answer: The fabric, lining and coverage around the opening all affect light control. We'll discuss how much darkness you need and review the arrangement, including light that may enter at the top, sides or bottom.

faqs.question: Can I add motorized control?
faqs.answer: Motorized drapery hardware is available for compatible arrangements. We'll review the fabric, hardware, opening and supported system before recommending an option.

sections.title: Start with the fabric and the room
paragraphs: Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to look at fabrics and discuss the windows you have in mind. We'll help you work through the style, lining and hardware choices, then arrange professional measuring.

name: Motorized Shades
title_tag: Motorized Shades in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Explore motorized shades in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Get help with PowerView, Somfy, compatible controls, professional installation and setup.

sections.title: Motorized Shades in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Adjust a tall window without reaching for it, or lower several shades together when the afternoon light changes. John and Max help you choose compatible motorized shades, install them and set up the controls. Visit our Woodland Hills showroom or call to discuss your rooms.

sections.title: Choose controls you'll want to use
paragraphs: Some customers like using an app. Others want a handheld remote or a control on the wall. We'll ask how you want to operate the shades and show you the options for the system you're considering.

You may want to adjust one shade at a time, operate several together or connect them to a smart-home system. The product and equipment determine which features are available, so we check those details before recommending a system.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas PowerView® Automation
paragraphs: PowerView® Automation operates compatible Hunter Douglas window treatments. We can help you compare the available products, remotes and app controls, along with any hub or gateway needed for the features you want.
If you'd like the shades to move at set times, we can discuss schedules in the PowerView® App. We'll show you how the selected system works and help you set up the controls at installation.
sections.disclosure: The PowerView® App is required for programmed operation.

sections.title: Somfy motorization
paragraphs: We also work with Somfy motorization on compatible window treatments. Depending on the motor and controls, options can include a handheld remote, a wall control and app access through compatible equipment.
If you're adding to motorized treatments you already own, let us know what equipment you have. We check the motor, controls and connected equipment together before recommending an addition.

sections.title: Plan the power supply before the order
paragraphs: Power choices depend on the product. Available options may include replaceable batteries, rechargeable power or a wired connection. For a tall window, the way you reach a battery or charger matters just as much as the control you choose.
For a new build or remodel, involve us while the wiring and window details can still be coordinated. If electrical work is needed, we can discuss the shade requirements with your electrician.

sections.title: A motorization job in Santa Rosa Valley
paragraphs: On a new-build project in Santa Rosa Valley, one of the connections for the hardwired shades wasn't working after the walls had been finished. We coordinated with an electrician to resolve the wiring issue, then completed the shade and app setup.
It is one reason we like to be involved early in a project. We install and set up the window treatments, with electrical work handled by the electrician.

sections.title: Help after the shades are installed
paragraphs: We'll show you how to use the controls before we finish. If something stops responding later, contact us and describe what's happening. Some questions can be worked through over the phone; others need a closer look.
John has helped customers recalibrate a shade through the app without needing a visit. What we can do depends on the system and the problem, so we'll work through that with you.

sections.title: Questions about motorized window treatments

faqs.question: Can you motorize shades I already have?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. The product, age, condition and available components determine what's possible. Send us the brand and model if you know them, along with photos, so we can review the options.

faqs.question: Will it work with my existing smart-home system?
faqs.answer: Compatibility depends on the motor, controls, generation and connected equipment. Tell us which system you use and we'll check the requirements. We don't assume every motorized product works with every platform.

faqs.question: Can I keep a remote as well as an app?
faqs.answer: Many systems support more than one control method. We'll confirm the combination available for your shades and show you how to use it.

sections.title: Talk with John and Max about motorization
paragraphs: Tell us which windows you'd like to operate more easily and whether you're starting with new shades or reviewing an existing system. We'll help you work through the product, controls, installation and setup.
